summary:
1. RF-DETR today is rfdetr 1.12.1 (PyPI, 2026-11-12, Apache-2.0): Python >=3.10, torch>=2.2, torchvision>=0.17, transformers>=5.1,<6, supervision>=0.29, pydantic 2. On paper it has no pin conflict with ultralytics 8.4.218 in one venv (not install-tested); the conflict only appears with rfdetr[stream] or dfine-seg, which pull opencv-python-headless against Ultralytics' opencv-python.
2. Current segmentation classes are RFDETRSegNano/Small/Medium/Large/XLarge/2XLarge, all Apache-2.0; RFDETRSegPreview and RFDETRBase are deprecated. Seg checkpoints are 134.5-154.9 MB each and cache in ~/.roboflow/models (env RF_HOME). Detection Nano/Small/Medium .pth files are 366-405 MB; the Hugging Face safetensors copies are 122-135 MB.
3. Inference is model.predict(rgb, threshold=..., shape=(H,W)) -> supervision.Detections with .mask as (N,H,W) bool. Fine-tuned weights load with RFDETRSegSmall(pretrain_weights=path) or rfdetr.from_checkpoint(path); class names come back in detections.data["class_name"].
4. MPS is supported and auto-detected; the old MPS bugs were closed in March 2026. The only official Apple numbers are for an M4 Max: RFDETRSmall 20.0 ms eager, 10.3 ms compiled. The base M4 is unmeasured; expect several times slower.
5. COCO weights are useless for cubes (no such class), so every model in this topic needs fine-tuning before it shows anything meaningful.
6. RF-DETR-Seg's weak point here is resolution: default input is 312-432 px, stretched to a square without letterbox, with mask logits at 1/4 of that. A 61 px cube gets about 4-5 mask cells across. Corners and angle need a square ROI crop and/or resolution 576-768.
7. D-FINE, DEIMv2, RT-DETRv2/v4 and LW-DETR output axis-aligned boxes only (no masks, no oriented boxes): skip. YOLOv12/v13 forks install as a package named ultralytics and shadow the real one: skip. RT-DETRv3 is PaddlePaddle: skip.
8. The only extra worth a slot is D-FINE-seg (pip dfine-seg 0.8.0, Apache-2.0, instance masks, 17 MB nano weights, MPS inference), as optional. LibreYOLO (MIT, one API including oriented-box variants) exists but is too sprawling and experimental for four days. Beyond that the honest answer is none.
9. With four days left, Ultralytics YOLO seg or OBB is the practical trainable choice; RF-DETR-Seg is the second, comparison entry. Label each cube's top face as a 4-corner polygon in YOLO txt: RF-DETR-Seg and D-FINE-seg read that format directly, and it should also serve YOLO-seg and YOLO-OBB (from memory, not re-read).
10. Disk: one RF-DETR training run writes many 130-400 MB checkpoints. Train on a free Colab T4 and bring back only checkpoint_best_total.pth.

candidates.family: RF-DETR-Seg (Roboflow, DINOv2 backbone + DETR decoder + mask head)
candidates.what: Instance segmentation, trainable. Fine-tune on top-face polygons with classes red/green/blue/wood; each detection returns class, box and a boolean mask at image size. Centre, angle (mod 90) and 4 corners come from cv2.minAreaRect / boxPoints on the mask. Classes in 1.12.1: RFDETRSegNano (312 px, 100 queries), RFDETRSegSmall (384, 100), RFDETRSegMedium (432, 200), RFDETRSegLarge (504, 200), RFDETRSegXLarge (624, 300), RFDETRSeg2XLarge (768, 300). RFDETRSegPreview is deprecated (removal in 2.0). There is no oriented-box task in the rfdetr package. Smallest recipe: pip install "rfdetr[train]", dataset in YOLO-seg layout (data.yaml + train/images, train/labels, valid/images, valid/labels; auto-detected), then model.train(...) with an integer batch_size ("auto" is CUDA-only).
candidates.fit_for_task: Usable only after fine-tuning; COCO weights have no cube class. Good: converges fast on small datasets, a learned mask can separate wood cubes on white PLA and ignore basket floors where colour thresholds struggle, Apache-2.0. Weak: input is stretched to a square at 312-432 px and mask logits are 1/4 of that, so a 61 px cube in a 1280x720 frame becomes about 15-20 px wide and 4-5 mask cells across. That is too coarse for corners. Mitigate by cropping frames to a square board ROI for both training and inference and by using resolution 576-768 (multiple of 24; 12 for Nano). At 720 px on a 720x720 crop a cube spans about 15 mask cells. Angle from minAreaRect on such masks is likely a few degrees off (my estimate). Second choice behind YOLO seg/OBB for a 4-day deadline.
candidates.weights_id: rf-detr-seg-nano.pt (https://repo.roboflow.com/rfdetr/rf-detr-seg-n-ft.pth); also rf-detr-seg-small.pt, rf-detr-seg-medium.pt; HF copies Roboflow/rf-detr-seg-nano|small|medium
candidates.mps: works. Device is auto-detected through torch.accelerator; device="mps" is accepted for predict and train. Historic MPS failures (#29, #223, #362, #622 'Unsupported Border padding mode' in seg training) were closed by PR #821 in March 2026. 1.12.0 made model.inference() compile with inductor on MPS by default. FP8 and batch_size="auto" are CUDA-only. No open MPS training issue found. Open issue #1599: seg class confidence swings strongly with few-pixel image shifts.
candidates.latency_note: Official Apple numbers exist only for an M4 Max (40-core GPU) and RFDETRSmall detection at 512 px, batch 1, end to end: predict() eager 20.0 ms, inference() TorchScript fp16 12.2 ms, inductor fp16 10.3 ms. Core ML RFDETRSegNano fp16 on the same machine: 38.8-44.2 ms. Nothing is published for a base M4 (10-core GPU) or for Seg under PyTorch MPS; my estimate is 40-100 ms per frame eager at 432-576 px. Training: an L4 does a 4-image RFDETRNano detection step in 171 ms, so 100 images x 50 epochs is minutes on an L4 and roughly 10-25 min on a free Colab T4 for Seg Nano/Small (estimate). On M4 MPS plan for 30-90 min (unmeasured).
candidates.ram_note: 33.6-35.7 M params (about 135-145 MB fp32). Estimate, not measured: 1.5-2.5 GB process RSS for inference including torch and transformers; model.inference() holds a second copy of the weights. Training at batch 2-4 and 432-576 px should fit in 16 GB unified memory, but with a 99% full disk macOS has little room to swap.
candidates.snippet:
import cv2, numpy as np, supervision as sv
import rfdetr
from rfdetr import RFDETRSegSmall  # RFDETRSegNano / RFDETRSegMedium

# --- train (pip install "rfdetr[train]"; YOLO-seg or COCO dataset dir) ---
m = RFDETRSegSmall(resolution=576)            # multiple of 24 (SegNano: 12)
m.train(dataset_dir="cubes", epochs=40, batch_size=2, grad_accum_steps=4,
        lr=1e-4, device="mps", num_workers=0, output_dir="runs/rfdetr_seg",
        checkpoint_interval=40, early_stopping=True, run_test=False)

# --- load fine-tuned weights ---
model = rfdetr.from_checkpoint("runs/rfdetr_seg/checkpoint_best_total.pth")  # restores class, resolution, class names
# or: RFDETRSegSmall(pretrain_weights="...pth", resolution=576)

bgr = cv2.imread("frame.jpg")
rgb = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)     # predict() expects RGB
det = model.predict(rgb, threshold=0.4, include_source_image=False)  # supervision.Detections
# det.xyxy (N,4), det.confidence (N,), det.class_id (N,), det.mask (N,H,W) bool, det.data["class_name"]
for mask, name in zip(det.mask, det.data["class_name"]):
    cnts, _ = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    (cx, cy), (w, h), ang = cv2.minAreaRect(max(cnts, key=cv2.contourArea))
    corners = cv2.boxPoints(((cx, cy), (w, h), ang)); angle = ang % 90
annotated = sv.MaskAnnotator().annotate(bgr.copy(), det)
# optional: shape=(432, 768) in predict() keeps 16:9 (each side divisible by patch_size*num_windows)

candidates.what: Box detector, trainable. Would act as a learned cube finder and R/G/B/wood classifier; angle and corners then need a classical step inside each box (threshold + minAreaRect). Classes: RFDETRNano (384 px), RFDETRSmall (512), RFDETRMedium (576), RFDETRLarge (704), resolution in multiples of 32, 300 queries. RFDETRAtto/Femto/Pico/XLarge/2XLarge need rfdetr[plus] and the PML 1.0 licence. The same weights also load through transformers 5.24.1 as RfDetrForObjectDetection from Roboflow/rf-detr-nano|small|medium.
candidates.fit_for_task: Axis-aligned boxes only, so it cannot give the angle or the top-face quad by itself. For a square of side s the box side is s(|cos t|+|sin t|), which leaves t and 90-t indistinguishable. Useful only as stage one of a two-stage pipeline, and the seg variant or YOLO-OBB does that job in one step. Also disk-hungry: the Nano/Small/Medium .pth downloads are 366-405 MB each. Needs fine-tuning.
candidates.licence: Apache-2.0 for Nano/Small/Medium/Large; PML 1.0 for Atto/Femto/Pico/XL/2XL (rfdetr[plus])
candidates.weights_id: rf-detr-nano.pth (366.3 MB), rf-detr-small.pth (386.0), rf-detr-medium.pth (405.0), rf-detr-large-2026.pth (136.0) from repo.roboflow.com/rfdetr; HF safetensors Roboflow/rf-detr-nano (121.9), -small (128.5), -medium (134.8)
candidates.mps: works; same code path and history as the seg variant
candidates.latency_note: M4 Max, RFDETRSmall, batch 1 end to end: 20.0 ms eager predict(), 10.3-12.2 ms compiled inference(). Base M4 unmeasured.
candidates.ram_note: 30.5-33.9 M params. Estimate 1.5-2 GB RSS for inference.

import cv2
from rfdetr import RFDETRSmall
model = RFDETRSmall(pretrain_weights="runs/det/checkpoint_best_total.pth")  # or RFDETRSmall() for COCO
rgb = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread("frame.jpg"), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

# transformers path (smaller download, cached in ~/.cache/huggingface/hub)

candidates.family: D-FINE-seg (ArgoHA; D-FINE detector + mask / keypoint heads, HGNetv2 CNN backbone)
candidates.what: Instance segmentation, detection, keypoints and semantic segmentation in one pip package with its own training CLI. Sizes n/s/m/l/x at 640 px with 1/4-resolution mask features. Fine-tune with task: segment on YOLO polygon labels (flat images/ + labels/ folders, split by `dfine split`); output is a dict with labels, boxes, scores and masks [N,H,W]. Also ships a small browser demo (`dfine demo`).
candidates.fit_for_task: The one non-Ultralytics, non-RF-DETR model that gives masks through a clean pip path. Attractive on this Mac: nano seg weights are 17 MB and the default 640 px input keeps a cube at about 30 px (60 px on a square ROI crop). Risks: version 0.8.0 with 14 releases so far and a small project (247 stars); heavy base dependencies (wandb, pandas, scikit-learn, albumentations, hydra); it requires opencv-python-headless, which collides with Ultralytics' opencv-python in a shared venv; training on MPS is not documented. Needs fine-tuning. Add it only if YOLO seg and RF-DETR-Seg are already working.
candidates.licence: Apache-2.0 code and COCO weights (the Cityscapes semantic weights are non-commercial)
candidates.weights_id: HF ArgoSA/D-FINE-seg: dfine_seg_n_coco.pt (17.1 MB), dfine_seg_s_coco.pt (48.1), dfine_seg_m_coco.pt (85.4); detection dfine_n_coco.pt (15.5)
candidates.mps: works for inference per README (Torch backend lists CUDA, MPS, CPU) and code (TorchModel auto-selects mps). Training on MPS: unknown, not documented.
candidates.latency_note: No Apple numbers published. README reports 1.9 ms engine / 3.1 ms end to end for S seg on an RTX 5070 Ti with TensorRT. `dfine hw_bench` measures torch throughput on mps.
candidates.ram_note: N is 3.4 M params, S about 12 M; the lightest option here. Estimate 1-1.5 GB RSS.

candidates.family: D-FINE / DEIMv2 / RT-DETRv2 / LW-DETR through Hugging Face transformers
candidates.what: Real-time DETR-style box detectors, all available in transformers 5.24.1 behind AutoModelForObjectDetection: DFineForObjectDetection (ustc-community/dfine-nano-coco 15.3 MB, dfine-small-coco 41.5 MB), Deimv2ForObjectDetection (harshaljanjani/DEIMv2_HGNetv2_N_COCO_Transformers 14.6 MB, DEIMv2_DINOv3_S_COCO_Transformers 39.4 MB), RTDetrV2ForObjectDetection (PekingU/rtdetr_v2_r18vd 80.9 MB), LwDetrForObjectDetection (AnnaZhang/lwdetr_tiny_60e_coco 48.3 MB). None is gated.
candidates.fit_for_task: Poor fit. Each of them exposes only an object-detection head: axis-aligned boxes, no instance masks, no oriented boxes. COCO weights do not know cubes, so they need fine-tuning too, and fine-tuning through the transformers Trainer is more code than rfdetr or Ultralytics. After all that you would still need a classical step for angle and corners. They add nothing over RF-DETR detection for this task.
candidates.licence: Apache-2.0 on the listed HF checkpoints; the upstream DEIMv2 repository uses its own 'DEIMv2 License'
candidates.pip_package: transformers==5.24.1 (Python >=3.11; already installed as an rfdetr dependency)
candidates.mps: unknown; plain PyTorch modules, not tested or documented for MPS in the pages read
candidates.latency_note: No Apple numbers. T4 TensorRT numbers in the RF-DETR README: D-FINE-N 2.1 ms, D-FINE-S 3.5 ms, LW-DETR-T 1.9 ms.
candidates.snippet:
import torch
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, AutoModelForObjectDetection
from transformers.image_utils import load_image

repo = "ustc-community/dfine-nano-coco"   # or harshaljanjani/DEIMv2_HGNetv2_N_COCO_Transformers, PekingU/rtdetr_v2_r18vd, AnnaZhang/lwdetr_tiny_60e_coco
image = load_image("frame.jpg")
proc = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(repo)
model = AutoModelForObjectDetection.from_pretrained(repo).to("mps")
inputs = proc(images=image, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
with torch.no_grad():
    out = model(**inputs)
res = proc.post_process_object_detection(out, target_sizes=[(image.height, image.width)], threshold=0.5)[0]
# res["scores"], res["labels"], res["boxes"] (xyxy); names via model.config.id2label

candidates.family: LibreYOLO (MIT wrapper library: YOLOv9, YOLOX, RF-DETR, D-FINE, DEIM/DEIMv2, RT-DETR v1/v2/v4, EdgeCrafter and many more)
candidates.what: One Ultralytics-style API (LibreYOLO(name)(image) -> Results with boxes, masks, obb.xywhr / obb.xyxyxyxy, keypoints) over re-implemented model families, with weights on the Hugging Face LibreYOLO organisation (465 repos). Relevant ones: LibreDFINEn-seg (17.1 MB), LibreRFDETRn-seg (134.5 MB .pt), LibreECs-seg (42.1 MB) and oriented-box variants LibreRTDETRv2n-obb (16.2 MB, DOTA), LibreRFDETRn-obb (121.4 MB, labelled 'ultra-experimental', CC BY 4.0), LibreRiODETRv2*-obb.
candidates.fit_for_task: It is the only non-Ultralytics pip path found that offers oriented boxes, which is exactly a cube's top-face quad. But the published OBB weights are aerial or vehicle models, so oriented-box training on cubes would be mandatory, and the RF-DETR OBB weights are self-described as ultra-experimental. The library is huge (151 families) and young, and I did not find MPS statements for the detection, seg or OBB paths. With four days left it is a risk, not a shortcut. Worth a look after the competition, or if Ultralytics OBB fails.
candidates.licence: MIT (library); weights carry their upstream licences (Apache-2.0, CC BY 4.0, ...)
candidates.pip_package: libreyolo==1.8.0 (2026-11-15; Python >=3.10; torch>=2.4; opencv-python>=4.11; RF-DETR family needs libreyolo[rfdetr] = transformers>=5.1.0)
candidates.mps: unknown for detect/segment/obb. The changelog mentions Apple MPS only for other families, and docs/rfdetr_training.md says the fast training paths exclude CPU/MPS.
candidates.ram_note: Depends on the family behind the name.
candidates.snippet:
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO
model = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLO/LibreDFINEn-seg")   # HF repo name, or a local .pt; RF-DETR names need pip install "libreyolo[rfdetr]"
r = model("frame.jpg")[0]                        # Ultralytics-style Results
# r.boxes.xyxy, r.masks, r.obb.xywhr, r.obb.xyxyxyxy, r.keypoints
# model.train(data="dataset.yaml", epochs=100, imgsz=640)

candidates.what: RFDETRKeypointPreview: box plus K keypoints per object, 576 px, 40.7 M params, pretrained on COCO person keypoints. Custom keypoint schemas are supported in fine-tuning (COCO keypoint JSON or YOLO pose labels with kpt_shape), so the 4 top-face corners could in principle be predicted directly as keypoints.
candidates.fit_for_task: Tempting but wrong for this deadline. A cube's corners are interchangeable under 90-degree rotation, so the keypoint order has to be canonicalised in the labels or training is ill-posed. The model is a preview, exists in one large size only, and its pretrained weights know people, not cubes. Masks or oriented boxes reach the same quad with less risk.
candidates.mps: unknown for the keypoint head specifically; the package supports MPS
candidates.latency_note: 9.7 ms on a T4 with TensorRT FP16 (README); no Apple numbers.
candidates.snippet:
from rfdetr import RFDETRKeypointPreview
model = RFDETRKeypointPreview()
kp = model.predict("image.jpg", threshold=0.5)   # supervision.KeyPoints: kp.xy, kp.data["xyxy"], kp.data["class_name"]

candidates.what: Forks of the Ultralytics code base. Installation is clone + pip install -r requirements.txt + pip install -e ., and the code is imported as `from ultralytics import YOLO`. YOLOv12 has a separate Seg branch with instance-segmentation models (released 2025-06-04). Neither has its own PyPI package (yolov12 and yolov13 return 404 on PyPI).
candidates.fit_for_task: Do not install. Each fork replaces the `ultralytics` module in the environment, so it cannot share a venv with the official package, and both install guides are built around flash-attn wheels for CUDA Linux. They give no capability the official package lacks: the Ultralytics docs index lists YOLO12 for detect/segment/classify/pose/OBB with pretrained weights for detection only. For 61 px cubes the architecture generation makes no practical difference.
candidates.licence: Not re-read in this run; presumably AGPL-3.0 inherited from Ultralytics
candidates.weights_id: GitHub release assets, e.g. yolov12n.pt from sunsmarterjie/yolov12 releases 'turbo'
candidates.snippet:
# not recommended; the official package covers the YOLO12 architecture:
from ultralytics import YOLO
model = YOLO("yolo12n.pt")

candidates.family: RT-DETRv3, RT-DETRv4, EdgeCrafter (ECDet / ECSeg / ECPose), upstream D-FINE and DEIMv2 repositories
candidates.what: Clone-and-run research code bases. RT-DETRv3 is PaddlePaddle. RT-DETRv4 (ECCV 2026) and upstream D-FINE / DEIMv2 are detection-only with conda + requirements.txt installs. EdgeCrafter (TMLR 2026, the DEIMv2 successor) adds instance segmentation (ECSeg-S 43.0 mask AP, 10 M params, HF Intellindust/ECSeg_S 41.9 MB) and pose, under its own 'EdgeCrafter License'.
candidates.fit_for_task: Not for a four-day student schedule: no pip-installable inference path, config-file driven training, the documented devices are cuda / xpu / cpu (no MPS mention), and custom licences on EdgeCrafter and DEIMv2. ECSeg is the only one with masks; if it ever matters it is reachable through LibreYOLO (LibreECs-seg).
candidates.licence: RT-DETRv4: see repo LICENSE (not read); D-FINE Apache-2.0; DEIMv2 'DEIMv2 License'; EdgeCrafter 'EdgeCrafter License' (commercial use by enquiry)
candidates.mps: unknown; README device option lists cuda / xpu / cpu only

packaging: rfdetr==1.12.1 (uploaded 2026-11-12). requires-python >=3.10. Core dependencies: requests, numpy, torch>=2.2.0, torchvision>=0.17.0, tqdm, transformers>=5.1.0,<6.0.0, pydantic>=2,<3, supervision>=0.29.0, pyDeprecate>=0.9,<0.10. Use Python 3.12: transformers 5.24.1 and torch 2.15.0 both require Python >=3.11.

Extras: rfdetr[train] adds pytorch_lightning>=2.6, torchmetrics[detection], pycocotools, faster-coco-eval, hotcoco, vernier, scipy, simplejpeg, peft, roboflow. rfdetr[stream] adds opencv-python-headless, mss, yt-dlp and is needed only for RFDETRInference on video/webcam sources. rfdetr[plus] adds the PML-1.0 models. rfdetr[augment] adds albumentations and kornia.

Sharing a venv with ultralytics 8.4.218 (numpy, matplotlib, opencv-python>=4.7, pillow, torch>=1.8, torchvision>=0.9, psutil, polars, ultralytics-thop, ultralytics-platform): no version pin collides with rfdetr's on paper. supervision 0.32.1 no longer depends on OpenCV (av>=14.2, scipy, matplotlib, pydeprecate>=0.9,<0.16). This was checked from PyPI metadata only; nothing was installed.

Real conflicts: rfdetr[stream] and dfine-seg both require opencv-python-headless, while ultralytics and libreyolo require opencv-python. The two wheels write the same cv2 module. Skip rfdetr[stream] (decode frames yourself with cv2 or PyAV and call model.predict per frame) and keep dfine-seg in its own venv or install it with care.
The Roboflow `inference` package (1.8.6) is not needed for local RF-DETR and pins supervision<0.31, numpy<2.4, opencv-python<4.13, pydantic<2.12. Do not add it to this environment.
transformers>=5.1 with huggingface-hub>=1.31 is forced by rfdetr. Any other model library that still pins transformers 4.x or huggingface_hub<1.0 cannot share the venv.

Wheel sizes for macOS arm64 / Python 3.12 (download, not installed size): torch 2.15.0 138.6 MB, torchvision 0.29.2 1.8 MB, transformers 5.24.1 13.6 MB, opencv-python 5.1.0.95 25.8 MB (macosx_15_0 tag), scipy 1.18.1 20.5 MB, av 19.0.2 18.6 MB, matplotlib 9.3 MB, numpy 5.5 MB. Expect roughly 1-1.5 GB installed for torch + rfdetr + ultralytics (my estimate).

Weight caches: rfdetr writes published checkpoints to ~/.roboflow/models; override with RF_HOME (alias ROBOFLOW_HOME). A bare filename in pretrain_weights resolves there; a path with a directory is used as given. Files download from https://repo.roboflow.com/rfdetr with MD5 validation; no token needed.

Weights loaded through transformers, and LibreYOLO weights, go to the shared Hugging Face cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub; HF_HOME moves it). dfine-seg also downloads from Hugging Face on first use; its cache location was not checked. None of the repos checked is gated, so no HF token is required.

RF-DETR checkpoint sizes (HTTP content-length): seg nano 134.5 MB, small 135.0, medium 143.0, large 145.1, xlarge 152.7, 2xlarge 154.9; detection nano 366.3, small 386.0, medium 405.0, large-2026 136.0; keypoint preview 163.7.

Training output directory (default ./output) receives last.ckpt, checkpoint_<epoch>.ckpt every checkpoint_interval epochs (default 10), checkpoint_best_ema.pth, checkpoint_best_regular.pth, checkpoint_best_total.pth, last_ema.pth and training_config.json. Keep only checkpoint_best_total.pth for inference.

One dataset for several trainers: RF-DETR auto-detects a YOLO dataset (data.yaml plus train/images + train/labels and valid/images + valid/labels, or images/train-style paths from the yaml) and reads YOLO-seg polygon lines (class x1 y1 x2 y2 ...). D-FINE-seg wants a flat images/ + labels/ folder with the same label lines and makes its own split.
pitfalls: Colour-channel order: rfdetr predict() expects RGB. Passing a cv2 BGR frame swaps red and blue, which silently breaks an R/G/B classifier. dfine-seg's read_image, by contrast, is BGR. Convert explicitly per model adapter.

RF-DETR resizes by stretching to the model resolution, with no letterbox, in both training and predict(). A 1280x720 frame at the default square resolution squashes cubes anisotropically (61 px becomes about 18x33 px at 384). Crop frames to a square board ROI for both training and inference, or pass shape=(H,W) with each side divisible by patch_size*num_windows (24 for Seg Small..2XL, 12 for Seg Nano, 32 for detection).

Mask resolution: mask logits are produced at 1/4 of the input resolution and bilinearly upsampled to the image, then thresholded at 0. At default Seg resolutions a cube covers only 4-9 mask cells per side, so minAreaRect corners are coarse.

Label the top face only. The camera is 601 mm up, so a 25 mm cube 300 mm off-axis shows about 30 px of side wall. A whole-silhouette label would bias the centre and the angle; a 4-corner top-face polygon keeps the target well defined.

antialias mismatch: predict(antialias=False) is the default and matches checkpoints trained with the Albumentations resize (used when rfdetr[augment] is installed). A checkpoint trained without rfdetr[augment] used torchvision antialiased resize and needs predict(..., antialias=True). The wrong setting causes silent accuracy drift, worst on small objects.

model.inference() compiles by default (inductor on MPS): several seconds on first use, fixed batch size and resolution, recompiles per input shape. For a lab that takes arbitrary uploads use model.predict() or model.inference(compile=False).

Disk: the detection Nano/Small/Medium downloads are 366-405 MB each, and one training run can leave more than 1 GB of checkpoints. With 5.7 GB free, download one variant at a time, raise checkpoint_interval, delete run folders, and prefer training on Colab.

batch_size="auto" probes CUDA memory and is rejected on MPS/CPU; pass an integer. grad_accum_steps now defaults to 1 (it was 4), so batch_size=4 is an effective batch of 4. FP8 and the cuda_graphs options are CUDA-only.

Class ids: COCO-pretrained RF-DETR returns sparse COCO category ids (1-90); fine-tuned models return 0-based ids. Read names from detections.data["class_name"] or model.class_names, not from COCO_CLASSES.

Old tutorials are stale: RFDETRBase, RFDETRSegPreview and RFDETRLargeDeprecated are deprecated since 1.7.0, optimize_for_inference() was removed in 1.11.0, and source_image moved from detections.data to detections.metadata.

Concurrency: before 1.11.2, several threads calling predict() on a cold model could corrupt its weights without an error. Pin >=1.11.2 and still serialise inference per model with a lock in the web server.

Open issue #1599: RF-DETR-Seg classification confidence can swing from about 0.9 to below 0.5 when the same image is shifted by a few pixels, while box and mask stay correct. Expect flicker on video near the threshold; use a low threshold plus temporal smoothing.

include_source_image=True is the default and copies every frame into the result; set it to False for video. Masks are (N,H,W) bool at full image size, so store polygons or minAreaRect results in run history, not raw masks.
Default RF-DETR training augmentation is scale jitter/crop plus horizontal flip. Any hue-shifting augmentation would corrupt colour classes; keep colour augmentation mild in every trainer.

Pretrained COCO checkpoints of all these models will show nothing useful on cubes (at best random 'book' or 'cell phone' boxes; that is my expectation, not tested). The lab should mark them as 'needs custom weights' instead of presenting an empty result as a model failure.
Time estimates in this report for the base M4 and for Colab T4 training are my extrapolations from published M4 Max and L4 numbers, not measurements.
open_questions: Real latency of RF-DETR-Seg Nano/Small at 576-768 px on the base M4 (10-core GPU) under PyTorch MPS, eager and compiled. No published number exists; it has to be measured in the lab.
Does model.inference() with the inductor backend compile on this machine (torch 2.15, macOS 15.7) without extra toolchain setup? Untested.
Does `uv pip install rfdetr==1.12.1 ultralytics` actually resolve and import cleanly on Python 3.12 arm64? The compatibility claim is from metadata only because installing was out of scope.
RF-DETR-Seg training speed and peak memory on M4 MPS at batch 2-4. Unmeasured; a Colab T4 run is the safer plan.
D-FINE-seg training on MPS is not documented, only inference. Its cache directory for auto-downloaded weights was not checked.
Mask-derived angle accuracy for a 61 px cube at each resolution is unknown until measured against labelled corners. Is a few degrees of error acceptable for the gripper?
The claim that a 4-point YOLO-seg polygon line is also a valid Ultralytics YOLO-OBB label line is from memory of the Ultralytics docs, not re-read in this run.
Label policy depends on unknowns in the brief: how many faces carry coloured paper, and whether the visible side wall of off-axis cubes has a different colour from the top.
Licence of the YOLOv12/YOLOv13 forks and of RT-DETRv4 was not read in this run.
torchvision Mask R-CNN (no extra dependency, 28x28 per-instance masks) was not researched; it could be a fallback segmenter if both YOLO-seg and RF-DETR-Seg disappoint.
